items.title: John L. Jones Interview, 1972-06-05
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Oscar Ruzon is taking a solo. [INTERVIEWEE] This boy is the bass player... [INTERVIEWER] Oscar Ruzon the uh. He was the leader. [INTERVIEWEE] He was the leader of that band.

ctx.x: That-that-that-that's-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh-uh- It was about eight years ago.
And Oscar Ruzon is taking a solo.

This boy is the bass player. He just played piano until Charlie Hampton come. Charlie Hampton was playing piano with Raymond Anker at that time. See the bass back in the back? That boy plays piano too. Oh what's his name? You know? I don't know. I'd look in that book. I'd look in my book to get his name. Yeah. He's a youngster.
